comparisons.title: Dermatomyositis vs Key Cutaneous Mimics
comparisons.subtitle: Clinical distribution is usually more discriminating than routine interface histology

values.dm: Gottron papules over MCP/IP joints; erythema can extend linearly between joints; periungual capillary change.
values.cle: ACLE often favors skin between joints and may spare the knuckles; chilblain/DLE variants can involve digits.
values.psoriasis: Well-demarcated scaly plaques may cover knuckles; nail pitting/onycholysis support psoriasis.
values.contact: Exposure-shaped eczematous plaques; dorsal hands common, often fissured or vesicular.

values.dm: Heliotrope; midfacial erythema often involves nasolabial folds; scalp pruritus/scale common.
values.cle: Malar ACLE classically spares nasolabial folds; DLE may scar; SCLE usually spares central face.
values.psoriasis: Hairline/scalp plaques; may involve brows/nasolabial areas as sebopsoriasis.
values.contact: Eyelids/face may be prominent; sharp exposure pattern, edema, itch, and episodic relation to products/sun.

values.dm: Often markedly pruritic or burning; weakness, myalgia, dysphagia, dyspnea, arthritis may coexist.
values.cle: Often asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic; systemic lupus features depend on subtype and patient.
values.psoriasis: Variable itch; joint pain, stiffness, enthesitis, or dactylitis may signal PsA.
values.contact: Pruritus is dominant; burning possible; improves with avoidance.

values.dm: Vacuolar interface dermatitis, dyskeratosis, lymphocytic inflammation, and mucin; not reliably separable from CLE.
values.cle: Interface change, basal injury, perivascular/periadnexal inflammation and mucin; DLE adds follicular plugging and scarring features.
values.psoriasis: Regular psoriasiform hyperplasia, parakeratosis, diminished granular layer, neutrophils in stratum corneum.
values.contact: Spongiotic dermatitis with variable vesiculation and eosinophils; chronic lesions may become psoriasiform.

values.dm: Nailfold examination, proximal strength/function, muscle enzymes/MRI, MSA phenotype, lung/cancer risk assessment.
values.cle: CLE subtype morphology, ANA/ENA/systemic evaluation, medication review for SCLE, scarring risk.
values.psoriasis: Full skin/nail exam, family history, PsA screen; biopsy if atypical.
values.contact: Exposure chronology, distribution, avoidance response, and patch testing.

citations.quote: Garg, Merola, and Fitzpatrick (eds.). Interdisciplinary Approaches to Overlap Disorders in Dermatology & Rheumatology. Springer, 2022.
Concha et al. review diagnostic and classification limitations in amyopathic dermatomyositis, including overlap with lupus.
European S2k guideline outlines topical, antimalarial, and subsequent systemic treatment strategies for cutaneous lupus erythematosus.

comparisons.title: Dermatomyositis MSA Phenotype Matrix
comparisons.subtitle: Associations guide surveillance; no antibody perfectly predicts an individual patient

values.mda5: Painful palmar papules, ulcerated Gottron lesions, lateral nailfold/digital ulcers, alopecia, oral pain/ulcers.
values.tif1: Extensive skin disease, poikiloderma, psoriasiform or hyperkeratotic lesions, palatal patch, red-on-white change.
values.nxp2: Often less striking skin relative to muscle; edema and calcinosis may dominate.
values.mi2: Classic prominent Gottron, heliotrope, shawl/V-sign phenotype.
values.sae: Severe skin-predominant onset; later myositis may develop.
values.antisyn: Mechanic’s hands, Raynaud; DM-specific rash may be absent or present.

values.mda5: Often amyopathic or less severe muscle disease.
values.nxp2: Often substantial weakness, myalgia, edema, dysphagia.
values.mi2: Classic proximal myositis, often treatment responsive.
values.sae: Myositis may follow initial skin disease; dysphagia can be prominent.
values.antisyn: Myositis ranges from absent/subclinical to severe.

values.mda5: High; rapidly progressive ILD is the defining emergency phenotype.
values.sae: Variable, usually not the dominant feature.
values.antisyn: High; ILD may precede or dominate muscle disease.

values.tif1: Strong association; use enhanced risk-stratified screening.
values.nxp2: Association reported; considered high risk in IMACS framework.
values.mi2: Lower than TIF1γ/NXP2 in most cohorts.
values.antisyn: Generally lower than classic cancer-associated DM phenotypes.

values.mda5: Do not be reassured by normal CK when ulcers/palmar papules and respiratory symptoms coexist.
values.tif1: Atypical extensive rash plus older age should accelerate malignancy workup.
values.nxp2: Dysphagia, edema, or severe weakness may be disproportionate to visible skin disease.
values.mi2: Classic morphology and favorable response are common but not guaranteed.
values.sae: Continue muscle surveillance after a skin-predominant presentation.
values.antisyn: The complete triad is unnecessary; isolated ILD plus mechanic’s hands can be the clue.

citations.quote: Myositis-specific autoantibodies define clinically useful dermatomyositis phenotypes, including MDA5, TIF1γ, NXP2, Mi-2, and SAE associations.
IMACS international guideline provides risk-stratified cancer screening recommendations for idiopathic inflammatory myopathies.
ACR/CHEST guideline conditionally recommends PFTs and HRCT for screening people with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases at risk for ILD.
